title: World in a Frame: Understanding Culture Mixing as a New Challenge for Vision-Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating food name and country-of-origin prediction accuracy using a Visual Question Answering (VQA) task on images containing mixed cultural elements (foods and backgrounds), and measuring prediction shifts toward distractor cultures or high-resource (WEIRD) countries.

Analyzing misclassification patterns in country-of-origin predictions to determine if models disproportionately favor high-resource countries (e.g., USA, India, China) over low-resource countries when identifying visual elements.
Comparing predicted labels before and after horizontally flipping multi-object images to assess if the spatial location (left vs. right) of an item affects model identification accuracy.
Evaluating whether changes in the relative size ratios of objects within multi-item images lead to differences in the model's identification accuracy.
